title: Roadblock Check Audit
eyebrow: Proposal · audit of the planned fix (parent issue #587), nothing built yet

short.lead: I tested the planned check against real transcripts and found eight weak spots; the fix keeps phrase matching as a cheap first layer and adds a record check and an optional model judge. You pick five options.
short.hint: Tap a card to see the evidence.
items: Seven things were tested, not guessed

I ran fixtures through the merged check, scanned 28 real final replies, timed a 5.3 MB transcript, and tried a model-judged Stop hook. Results are on the eight cards below. Anything I could not measure is labelled as reasoned.

items.caption: Measured items and reasoned items are labelled apart on each card.

items: Three layers instead of one phrase list

Layer 1 is the cheap phrase scan. Layer 2 reads the transcript record: three failed attempts by different method classes, all about one target, all listed in the reply. Layer 3 is an optional model judge that catches wording no list covers.

items.caption: Each layer covers a gap in the one before it.

items: You approve the audit and your five picks
Your approval is recorded in the decisions log, and the plan page is updated to match.
Pick one option for each question, then tap Copy my reply and paste it into this chat.

changes: chg
1. Claim wording slips past
Curly apostrophes, paraphrases and blockquotes.

Measured: a claim with a curly apostrophe (can’t) was not flagged, and a quoted blockquote line was flagged by mistake. Reasoned: a phrase list never covers every paraphrase, such as "wasn't able to" or "no way to".
Today the pattern needs a straight apostrophe and ignores only quotes and backticks.
Normalise apostrophes, ignore blockquotes and code, and add the optional model judge for paraphrases.
Fewer misses and fewer false alarms.
chg
2. The probe test is too loose
Any command containing ls, where, npm, pip or apt counted.
Measured: a turn that ran git ls-files counted as a probe, so the claim went through. This was the main cause on your PC.
Today a probe is any Bash command containing one of nine words.
Count only failed attempts that are about the claimed target, by method class.
A claim needs real evidence, not a lucky word.
chg
3. Other tools are invisible
PowerShell and MCP tool calls are not recognised.
Measured: after a PowerShell call to Get-Command, the claim was blocked, and after a failed MCP tool call it was blocked too. Whether your PC uses the PowerShell tool is unverified.
Today only the tool named Bash is read.
Read every tool's result, and add the Windows equivalents of each method class.
No false blocks on Windows or on MCP tools.
chg
4. What counts as failed
Errors, refusals and exit codes are mixed.

Measured in this session: the is_error flag is reliable (9 of 224 results), but it is also set by hook refusals and by harmless non-zero exits such as git commit with nothing to commit. Four results looked like failures with is_error unset.
Today failure is not read at all.
Failed means is_error, minus hook refusals and a short list of harmless exits, plus exit-0 results with strong failure text.
Evidence rests on real failures.
chg
5. The two fallbacks were weak
Unnamed target, and fewer than three methods.

Reasoned: counting any three failed results lets unrelated failures satisfy the rule, and "say why" is unchecked. Replacement: the three attempts must share a target word that also appears in the reply or your request, and a reason for fewer than three is checked by the model judge.
Today both fallbacks are in the plan as known weaknesses.
Shared-target relatedness, a closed table of method classes, and a judge-checked reason.
Unrelated failures no longer count.
chg
6. False alarms
Honest uncertainty, meta talk, subagents and real stops.

Measured: next step appeared in 2 of 28 real final replies, and one hit was a reply discussing the rule itself. Reasoned: a reply relaying a subagent's failure, or needing a licence, login or purchase, is a legitimate stop.
Today every phrase hit blocks up to twice.
Stall phrases need hand-back wording too, a marked exemption for licence, login, purchase and destructive stops, and the cap of two stays.
Fewer pointless blocks.
chg
7. The turn window and counter
Non-human messages reset them.

Measured: 2 of 17 messages counted as genuine in this session were system-reminder carriers, not you. A reset hides earlier attempts and changes the block counter's key. Hook feedback is correctly excluded.
Today any message not on a short exclusion list is genuine.
Also exclude system-reminder carriers.
Attempts before the block keep counting.
chg
8. The environment
Mode field, other modes and speed.

Measured: the Stop payload has permission_mode, the whole Stop handler took 0.8 s on a 5.3 MB transcript, and the check itself adds 0.08 s. Estimate, not measured: 100 MB would take about 15 s. Hook time limits are unknown.
Today a missing mode is not handled and the whole file is read.
Announce a missing mode and treat it as present-in-room, read only the transcript's tail, and ask in question 5 about the auto and dontAsk modes.
Safe on long sessions.
choices: first
How much checking sits behind the phrase scan?
A
Layers 1 and 2 only: phrase scan plus the record check, no model call
Free and fast, but wording no list covers still slips through.
B
Add layer 3: a model-judged Stop hook on every turn end (my suggestion)
Measured once: the judge flagged the claim, gave an actionable reason, and passed after methods were listed. Its call cost $0.004 for two evaluations, against $0.244 for the main model in that run.
C
Add layer 3 as an agent hook that reads the transcript itself
Strongest, since it can verify each listed method really ran, but it is slower and costs more. Not tested.
B closes the wording gap for a tiny measured cost. One run is a small sample, so the cost is an estimate.
second
How is a different method decided?
A
A closed table of method classes: existence check, disk search, package database, run it, ask the environment, other tool (my suggestion)
Three attempts must fall in three classes, so which, where and command -v count once.
B
A different command program or tool name
Simpler, but three existence checks would count as three methods.
A stops the cheapest way of gaming the rule.
third
What about stops that are really yours to settle?
A
The reply marks NEEDS YOU for a licence, login, purchase or destructive step, and is exempt from the three-attempt rule (my suggestion)
Matches the rule that those four stay yours. In unattended mode the work carries on elsewhere.
B
No exemption: the cap of two handles it
Simplest, but the agent is told to try again at things it can never do.
A keeps the block for real roadblocks only.
fourth
When do stall phrases such as next step flag a reply?
A
Only with hand-back wording too: ends in a question, or says your call, let me know, or waiting for you (my suggestion)
Cuts the 2 of 28 noise from ordinary next-step lines.
B
On the phrase alone, as approved
Catches more, but flags ordinary replies in unattended runs.
A still catches the Castle reply, which ended with "Your call".
fifth
Which permission modes count as no one is watching?
A
Unattended runs and bypassPermissions only, as approved (my suggestion)
Matches your answer exactly.
B
Also auto and dontAsk
Those modes also run without a person confirming each step, but you did not name them.
A keeps to your answer. B is one line to add later.

wrapup.summary: This audit found eight weak spots in the planned check and proposes three layers: phrases, a record check of three related failed attempts, and an optional model judge.
wrapup.changing: The claim pattern, the evidence test, the failure rule, the window rule and the plan page for issues #588 to #590.
wrapup.blocking: Your pick for each of the five questions under Your choices.
